passage:
A riverbank had been covered with concrete for many years. It prevented some flooding, but it also made the river fast and lifeless.
The city restored one section with plants, stones, and gentle slopes. At first, the area looked unfinished. Then insects, birds, and small fish returned.
Residents began walking there in the evening.
Engineers explained that rivers need space to slow down and breathe. A river is not just water that must be pushed away quickly.
The restored bank taught the city a different kind of control. Working with nature can sometimes protect people better than forcing nature into straight lines.
